{{c|{{sc|Chap. X.}}}}

''4. Permitted.'') {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Toleration and permission of euil.}}Some things are permitted, though not approued or allowed, to auoid greater inconueniences. No man may doe euil for any cause, but he may permit other mens euils for diuerse causes: as God him self doeth, who can doe no euil. So doth the Prince and Common-wealth permit lesser euils to eschew greater, and so may the Holy Church much more (as S. Augustine {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Aug. ep. 119 c. 19.''}}saith she doeth) being placed among much chaffe and much cockle, tolerate many things: and yet whatsoeuer is against faith and good life, she neither approueth, nor dissembleth with silence, nor committeth.

''11. And marrieth an other.'') That which S. Matthew vttered more obscurely, and is mistaken of some, as though he meant that for fornication a man might put away his wife and marry an other, is here by this Euangelist (as also by S. Luke) {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 16, 18.''}}put out of doubt, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Mariage after diuorce vnlawful.}}generally auouching, that whosoeuer putteth away his wife and marrieth an other, committeth aduoutrie. ''Aug. li. 1 de adult. coniug. c. 11 & sequentibus''.

''18. None is good.'') None is entirely, substantially, and of him self good, but God: though by participation of Gods goodnes, men are truely also called good.

''25. A riche man.'') He is here called a rich man that hath his confidence (as here is expressed) in his treasure, and had rather forsake his faith and duty to God, then lose them. as al they which liue in Schisme or Heresie to saue their goods.

''30. An hundred times so much.'') {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Their reward in this life that forsake ought for Gods sake.}}Sometime God doth so blesse men also in worldly benefites that haue forsaken al for him, as S. Gregorie, S. Augustine, and S. Paulinus: but the principal meaning is, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Hiero. in 19 Mat''.}}* that he wil giue to such men in this life aboundance of grace and spiritual comfort and contentatiō and ioy of cōscience (as they feele which haue experience) the which spiritual giftes excede the temporal commodities more then an hundred fold. in so much that he that hath fully forsaken but smal things for religion, would not forsake religion to haue al the world.

{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text={{sc|The}} fourth part of this Gospel, the {{sc|Holy}} weeke of his Passion in Hierusalem.}}{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XI.}}}}}}

{{c|''Being novv come to the place of his Passion, he entreth with triumph as their Christ. 12 He curseth that fruitlesse leafie tree. 15 He sheweth his Zeale for the house of God: for which the Rulers seeke his destruction. 24 He exhorteth his Disciples to stedfastnes of faith, and to forgiue their enemies. 27 He auoucheth his power by the witnes of Iohn who was a man sent of God.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=11|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=PALME Sunday.}}vvhen they came nigh vnto Hierusalem and Bethania to Mount-oliuet, he sendeth tvvo of his Disciples,{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 21, 1. Lu. 19, 20. Io. 12, 15.''}} {{verse|chapter=11|verse=2}}† and saith to them, Goe into the tovvne that is against you, and immediatly entring in thither, you shal finde a colt tied, vpon vvhich no man yet hath sitten: loose him, and bring him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=3}}† And if any man shal say to you, VVhat doe you? say that he is needeful for our Lord: and incontinent he vvil send him hither. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=4}}† And going their vvaies, they found the colt tied before the gate vvithout in the meeting of tvvo vvaies: and they loose him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=5}}† And certaine of them that stoode there, said to them, VVhat doe you loosing the colt? {{verse|chapter=11|verse=6}}† Vvho said to them as {{sc|Iesvs}} had commaunded them: and they did let him goe vvith them. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=7}}† And they brought the colt to {{sc|Iesvs}}: and they lay their garments vpon him, and he sate vpon him. {{verse|chapter=11|verse=8}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ Al these voluntary dueties were grateful to our Sauiour, and so be the like done to him in the B. Sacrament.}}∷ many spred their garments in the vvay:<noinclude>{{rh|||and}}</noinclude>
